We read 12 of the 37 executive orders we indexed, and the index continues past what we walked.

records.text: National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2027 (H R 8800): The yearly military policy bill. It says what the Department of Defense (and the Energy Department's nuclear-weapons programs) may spend money on for the 2027 budget year — which aircraft and ships to buy, how many people serve in the military, pay and health care rules for troops, how the Pentagon buys things, how it works with other countries, and rules for cybersecurity and artificial intelligence. Basis: Congressional Research Service summary, version updated 2026-06-29, read at the bill page.
records.sourceOrg: Congressional Research Service

records.text: Main Street Capital Access Act (H R 6955): Loosens rules on banks. New banks get three years to build up their required financial cushion, some rural banks can hold a smaller cushion, regulators must weigh how much their rules burden banks, and several size limits move up so more banks are exempt from fees, reports, and merger approvals — including letting some bank mergers go ahead without checking whether they reduce competition. Basis: Congressional Research Service summary, version updated 2026-07-20, read at the bill page.
records.sourceOrg: Congressional Research Service

records.text: Continuing Appropriations Act, 2027 (H R 9770): A stop-gap spending bill. It keeps the federal government funded — mostly at last year's levels — until December 4, 2026, or until the regular spending bills pass, whichever comes first. Without it the government would shut down when the budget year starts October 1. It makes exceptions for a few programs (like WIC food aid, disaster relief, the Indian Health Service, and wildfire fighting) and extends several expiring programs, including flood insurance. Basis: Congressional Research Service summary, version updated 2026-07-29, read at the bill page.
records.sourceOrg: Congressional Research Service

records.text: Stop Insider Trading Act (H R 7008): Bars members of Congress — and their spouses and dependent children — from buying stock in individual companies, and requires public notice 7 to 14 days before they sell stock they already own. Broad investments like widely held funds are exempt. Breaking the rules brings a fine of at least $2,000 or 10% of the trade (plus any profit made), which can't be paid with campaign money. Basis: Congressional Research Service summary, version updated 2026-07-17, read at the bill page.
records.sourceOrg: Congressional Research Service

records.text: Congressional budget for fiscal year 2027 (H CON RES 113): Congress's budget blueprint for 2027 (with targets through 2036). It doesn't spend money itself — it sets the overall numbers for spending, taxes, and debt, and tells four House committees to write follow-up legislation allowed to increase the deficit by set amounts. That follow-up uses a fast-track process the Senate can't filibuster. Basis: Congressional Research Service summary, version updated 2026-07-30, read at the bill page.
records.sourceOrg: Congressional Research Service

records.text: War Powers resolution on hostilities against Iran (H CON RES 89): Orders the President to pull U.S. armed forces out of hostilities against Iran unless Congress declares war or votes to authorize the use of military force. It says this doesn't stop the U.S. from defending itself, its forces, its diplomatic buildings, or allies from imminent attack. Basis: Congressional Research Service summary, version updated 2026-04-27, read at the bill page.
records.sourceOrg: Congressional Research Service

records.text: Removing Barriers to Work for Disabled Americans Act (H R 8884): Lets the Social Security Administration restart pilot programs — paused since 2022 — that test changes to disability benefits meant to help people on disability work more without losing income. Joining a pilot is voluntary, a participant's total income can't go down because of it, and the agency must tell Congress about each pilot 120 days before starting it. Basis: Congressional Research Service summary, version updated 2026-06-26, read at the bill page.
records.sourceOrg: Congressional Research Service

The CARES Act (March 2020): The first pandemic relief law: $1,200 payments to most adults, expanded unemployment benefits, and forgivable loans to keep small businesses paying staff. Selection criteria: Major legislation that became law (plus one pending measure, marked), and consequential Senate confirmations, since 2020 — chosen before looking at how anyone voted.
records.sourceOrg: congress.gov bill text and official summary

records.text: The American Rescue Plan (March 2021): The second big pandemic package: $1,400 payments, an expanded child tax credit that paid parents monthly for a year, and money for vaccines, schools and state governments. Selection criteria: Major legislation that became law (plus one pending measure, marked), and consequential Senate confirmations, since 2020 — chosen before looking at how anyone voted.
records.sourceOrg: congress.gov bill text and official summary

records.text: The Infrastructure Investment and Jobs Act (2021): About $550 billion in new money for roads, bridges, water pipes, rural broadband and the electric grid, spread over five years. Selection criteria: Major legislation that became law (plus one pending measure, marked), and consequential Senate confirmations, since 2020 — chosen before looking at how anyone voted.
records.sourceOrg: congress.gov bill text and official summary

records.text: The Bipartisan Safer Communities Act (2022): The first major federal gun law in about 30 years — tougher checks for buyers under 21, money for state red-flag programs and school mental health. Still in effect; the under-21 provisions expire in 2032 by the law's own terms. Selection criteria: Major legislation that became law (plus one pending measure, marked), and consequential Senate confirmations, since 2020 — chosen before looking at how anyone voted.
records.sourceOrg: congress.gov bill text and official summary

records.text: The CHIPS and Science Act (2022): About $52 billion to pay companies to build computer-chip factories in the United States, after the pandemic showed how much depends on chips made elsewhere. Selection criteria: Major legislation that became law (plus one pending measure, marked), and consequential Senate confirmations, since 2020 — chosen before looking at how anyone voted.
records.sourceOrg: congress.gov bill text and official summary

records.text: The Honoring our PACT Act (2022): Extended VA health care and disability benefits to veterans exposed to burn pits and other toxic hazards, and made the government presume certain illnesses were service-related instead of making each veteran prove it. Selection criteria: Major legislation that became law (plus one pending measure, marked), and consequential Senate confirmations, since 2020 — chosen before looking at how anyone voted.
records.sourceOrg: congress.gov bill text and official summary

records.text: The Inflation Reduction Act (2022): Let Medicare negotiate the price of some prescription drugs and capped insulin at $35 a month for people on Medicare, alongside tax credits for clean energy, paid for partly by a minimum tax on large corporations. Selection criteria: Major legislation that became law (plus one pending measure, marked), and consequential Senate confirmations, since 2020 — chosen before looking at how anyone voted.
records.sourceOrg: congress.gov bill text and official summary

records.text: The Respect for Marriage Act (2022): Requires every state to recognize same-sex and interracial marriages performed in other states, so those marriages stay valid even if the Supreme Court changes course. Selection criteria: Major legislation that became law (plus one pending measure, marked), and consequential Senate confirmations, since 2020 — chosen before looking at how anyone voted.
records.sourceOrg: congress.gov bill text and official summary

records.text: The Fiscal Responsibility Act (2023): Ended the debt-ceiling standoff by suspending the borrowing limit into 2025, in exchange for caps on federal spending and new work requirements for some food-stamp recipients. Selection criteria: Major legislation that became law (plus one pending measure, marked), and consequential Senate confirmations, since 2020 — chosen before looking at how anyone voted.
records.sourceOrg: congress.gov bill text and official summary

records.text: April 2024: aid to Ukraine: About $61 billion for Ukraine's defense against Russia's invasion — weapons, ammunition, and economic support. Selection criteria: Major legislation that became law (plus one pending measure, marked), and consequential Senate confirmations, since 2020 — chosen before looking at how anyone voted.
records.sourceOrg: congress.gov bill text and official summary

records.text: April 2024: aid to Israel and humanitarian aid for Gaza: About $26 billion for Israel's military and air defenses, including roughly $9 billion for humanitarian relief in Gaza and other conflict zones. Selection criteria: Major legislation that became law (plus one pending measure, marked), and consequential Senate confirmations, since 2020 — chosen before looking at how anyone voted.
records.sourceOrg: congress.gov bill text and official summary

records.text: April 2024: Indo-Pacific and Taiwan: About $8 billion for military support to Taiwan and other allies in the Indo-Pacific, and for U.S. submarine production. Selection criteria: Major legislation that became law (plus one pending measure, marked), and consequential Senate confirmations, since 2020 — chosen before looking at how anyone voted.
records.sourceOrg: congress.gov bill text and official summary

records.text: April 2024: TikTok divest-or-ban, and sanctions: Required TikTok's Chinese owner to sell the app or have it blocked in U.S. app stores, and added sanctions on Russia, Iran and their weapons suppliers. Selection criteria: Major legislation that became law (plus one pending measure, marked), and consequential Senate confirmations, since 2020 — chosen before looking at how anyone voted.
records.sourceOrg: congress.gov bill text and official summary

records.text: The Social Security Fairness Act (2025): Repealed two rules that reduced Social Security for millions of retired teachers, police, and other public workers, raising their monthly benefits. Selection criteria: Major legislation that became law (plus one pending measure, marked), and consequential Senate confirmations, since 2020 — chosen before looking at how anyone voted.
records.sourceOrg: congress.gov bill text and official summary

records.text: The Laken Riley Act (2025): Requires federal immigration authorities to detain people in the country illegally who are arrested for theft or certain violent crimes, and lets states sue the federal government over immigration enforcement decisions. Selection criteria: Major legislation that became law (plus one pending measure, marked), and consequential Senate confirmations, since 2020 — chosen before looking at how anyone voted.
records.sourceOrg: congress.gov bill text and official summary

records.text: The One Big Beautiful Bill Act (2025): Made the 2017 income-tax rates permanent and added new deductions, while cutting Medicaid and food-stamp spending through tighter eligibility and work rules, and increasing immigration-enforcement funding. Selection criteria: Major legislation that became law (plus one pending measure, marked), and consequential Senate confirmations, since 2020 — chosen before looking at how anyone voted.
records.sourceOrg: congress.gov bill text and official summary

records.text: The GENIUS Act (2025): The first federal rulebook for stablecoins — digital tokens meant to hold a fixed dollar value — requiring issuers to hold real dollar reserves and submit to federal or state supervision. Selection criteria: Major legislation that became law (plus one pending measure, marked), and consequential Senate confirmations, since 2020 — chosen before looking at how anyone voted.
records.sourceOrg: congress.gov bill text and official summary

records.text: The shutdown and the 2026 appropriations that ended it: Reopened the federal government after the longest shutdown on record and funded it for the rest of the year, restoring back pay to federal workers and resuming paused federal payments. Selection criteria: Major legislation that became law (plus one pending measure, marked), and consequential Senate confirmations, since 2020 — chosen before looking at how anyone voted.
records.sourceOrg: congress.gov bill text and official summary

records.text: The 21st Century ROAD to Housing Act (2025): The first broad federal housing law in years: money and rule changes aimed at getting more homes built, plus changes to rental assistance and homelessness programs. Selection criteria: Major legislation that became law (plus one pending measure, marked), and consequential Senate confirmations, since 2020 — chosen before looking at how anyone voted.
records.sourceOrg: congress.gov bill text and official summary

records.text: Banning members of Congress from trading individual stocks: Would bar members of Congress, and in most versions their spouses, from buying and selling individual company shares while in office, requiring blind trusts or divestment instead. This measure is pending. Selection criteria: Major legislation that became law (plus one pending measure, marked), and consequential Senate confirmations, since 2020 — chosen before looking at how anyone voted.

records.text: National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2027 (H R 8800): The yearly military policy bill. It says what the Department of Defense (and the Energy Department's nuclear-weapons programs) may spend money on for the 2027 budget year — which aircraft and ships to buy, how many people serve in the military, pay and health care rules for troops, how the Pentagon buys things, how it works with other countries, and rules for cybersecurity and artificial intelligence. Basis: Congressional Research Service summary, version updated 2026-06-29, read at the bill page.
records.sourceOrg: Congressional Research Service

records.text: Main Street Capital Access Act (H R 6955): Loosens rules on banks. New banks get three years to build up their required financial cushion, some rural banks can hold a smaller cushion, regulators must weigh how much their rules burden banks, and several size limits move up so more banks are exempt from fees, reports, and merger approvals — including letting some bank mergers go ahead without checking whether they reduce competition. Basis: Congressional Research Service summary, version updated 2026-07-20, read at the bill page.
records.sourceOrg: Congressional Research Service

records.text: Continuing Appropriations Act, 2027 (H R 9770): A stop-gap spending bill. It keeps the federal government funded — mostly at last year's levels — until December 4, 2026, or until the regular spending bills pass, whichever comes first. Without it the government would shut down when the budget year starts October 1. It makes exceptions for a few programs (like WIC food aid, disaster relief, the Indian Health Service, and wildfire fighting) and extends several expiring programs, including flood insurance. Basis: Congressional Research Service summary, version updated 2026-07-29, read at the bill page.
records.sourceOrg: Congressional Research Service

records.text: Stop Insider Trading Act (H R 7008): Bars members of Congress — and their spouses and dependent children — from buying stock in individual companies, and requires public notice 7 to 14 days before they sell stock they already own. Broad investments like widely held funds are exempt. Breaking the rules brings a fine of at least $2,000 or 10% of the trade (plus any profit made), which can't be paid with campaign money. Basis: Congressional Research Service summary, version updated 2026-07-17, read at the bill page.
records.sourceOrg: Congressional Research Service

records.text: Congressional budget for fiscal year 2027 (H CON RES 113): Congress's budget blueprint for 2027 (with targets through 2036). It doesn't spend money itself — it sets the overall numbers for spending, taxes, and debt, and tells four House committees to write follow-up legislation allowed to increase the deficit by set amounts. That follow-up uses a fast-track process the Senate can't filibuster. Basis: Congressional Research Service summary, version updated 2026-07-30, read at the bill page.
records.sourceOrg: Congressional Research Service

records.text: War Powers resolution on hostilities against Iran (H CON RES 89): Orders the President to pull U.S. armed forces out of hostilities against Iran unless Congress declares war or votes to authorize the use of military force. It says this doesn't stop the U.S. from defending itself, its forces, its diplomatic buildings, or allies from imminent attack. Basis: Congressional Research Service summary, version updated 2026-04-27, read at the bill page.
records.sourceOrg: Congressional Research Service

records.text: Removing Barriers to Work for Disabled Americans Act (H R 8884): Lets the Social Security Administration restart pilot programs — paused since 2022 — that test changes to disability benefits meant to help people on disability work more without losing income. Joining a pilot is voluntary, a participant's total income can't go down because of it, and the agency must tell Congress about each pilot 120 days before starting it. Basis: Congressional Research Service summary, version updated 2026-06-26, read at the bill page.
records.sourceOrg: Congressional Research Service

records.text: The CARES Act (March 2020): The first pandemic relief law: $1,200 payments to most adults, expanded unemployment benefits, and forgivable loans to keep small businesses paying staff. Selection criteria: Major legislation that became law (plus one pending measure, marked), and consequential Senate confirmations, since 2020 — chosen before looking at how anyone voted.
records.sourceOrg: congress.gov bill text and official summary

records.text: The American Rescue Plan (March 2021): The second big pandemic package: $1,400 payments, an expanded child tax credit that paid parents monthly for a year, and money for vaccines, schools and state governments. Selection criteria: Major legislation that became law (plus one pending measure, marked), and consequential Senate confirmations, since 2020 — chosen before looking at how anyone voted.
records.sourceOrg: congress.gov bill text and official summary

records.text: The Infrastructure Investment and Jobs Act (2021): About $550 billion in new money for roads, bridges, water pipes, rural broadband and the electric grid, spread over five years. Selection criteria: Major legislation that became law (plus one pending measure, marked), and consequential Senate confirmations, since 2020 — chosen before looking at how anyone voted.
records.sourceOrg: congress.gov bill text and official summary

records.text: The Bipartisan Safer Communities Act (2022): The first major federal gun law in about 30 years — tougher checks for buyers under 21, money for state red-flag programs and school mental health. Still in effect; the under-21 provisions expire in 2032 by the law's own terms. Selection criteria: Major legislation that became law (plus one pending measure, marked), and consequential Senate confirmations, since 2020 — chosen before looking at how anyone voted.

records.text: The CHIPS and Science Act (2022): About $52 billion to pay companies to build computer-chip factories in the United States, after the pandemic showed how much depends on chips made elsewhere. records.text: National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2027 (H R 8800): The yearly military policy bill. It says what the Department of Defense (and the Energy Department's nuclear-weapons programs) may spend money on for the 2027 budget year — which aircraft and ships to buy, how many people serve in the military, pay and health care rules for troops, how the Pentagon buys things, how it works with other countries, and rules for cybersecurity and artificial intelligence. Basis: Congressional Research Service summary, version updated 2026-06-29, read at the bill page.
records.sourceOrg: Congressional Research Service

records.text: Main Street Capital Access Act (H R 6955): Loosens rules on banks. New banks get three years to build up their required financial cushion, some rural banks can hold a smaller cushion, regulators must weigh how much their rules burden banks, and several size limits move up so more banks are exempt from fees, reports, and merger approvals — including letting some bank mergers go ahead without checking whether they reduce competition. Basis: Congressional Research Service summary, version updated 2026-07-20, read at the bill page.
records.sourceOrg: Congressional Research Service

records.text: Continuing Appropriations Act, 2027 (H R 9770): A stop-gap spending bill. It keeps the federal government funded — mostly at last year's levels — until December 4, 2026, or until the regular spending bills pass, whichever comes first. Without it the government would shut down when the budget year starts October 1. It makes exceptions for a few programs (like WIC food aid, disaster relief, the Indian Health Service, and wildfire fighting) and extends several expiring programs, including flood insurance. Basis: Congressional Research Service summary, version updated 2026-07-29, read at the bill page.
records.sourceOrg: Congressional Research Service

records.text: Stop Insider Trading Act (H R 7008): Bars members of Congress — and their spouses and dependent children — from buying stock in individual companies, and requires public notice 7 to 14 days before they sell stock they already own. Broad investments like widely held funds are exempt. Breaking the rules brings a fine of at least $2,000 or 10% of the trade (plus any profit made), which can't be paid with campaign money. Basis: Congressional Research Service summary, version updated 2026-07-17, read at the bill page.
records.sourceOrg: Congressional Research Service

records.text: Congressional budget for fiscal year 2027 (H CON RES 113): Congress's budget blueprint for 2027 (with targets through 2036). It doesn't spend money itself — it sets the overall numbers for spending, taxes, and debt, and tells four House committees to write follow-up legislation allowed to increase the deficit by set amounts. That follow-up uses a fast-track process the Senate can't filibuster. Basis: Congressional Research Service summary, version updated 2026-07-30, read at the bill page.
records.sourceOrg: Congressional Research Service

records.text: War Powers resolution on hostilities against Iran (H CON RES 89): Orders the President to pull U.S. armed forces out of hostilities against Iran unless Congress declares war or votes to authorize the use of military force. It says this doesn't stop the U.S. from defending itself, its forces, its diplomatic buildings, or allies from imminent attack. Basis: Congressional Research Service summary, version updated 2026-04-27, read at the bill page.
records.sourceOrg: Congressional Research Service

records.text: Removing Barriers to Work for Disabled Americans Act (H R 8884): Lets the Social Security Administration restart pilot programs — paused since 2022 — that test changes to disability benefits meant to help people on disability work more without losing income. Joining a pilot is voluntary, a participant's total income can't go down because of it, and the agency must tell Congress about each pilot 120 days before starting it. Basis: Congressional Research Service summary, version updated 2026-06-26, read at the bill page.
records.sourceOrg: Congressional Research Service

records.text: National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2027 (H R 8800): The yearly military policy bill. It says what the Department of Defense (and the Energy Department's nuclear-weapons programs) may spend money on for the 2027 budget year — which aircraft and ships to buy, how many people serve in the military, pay and health care rules for troops, how the Pentagon buys things, how it works with other countries, and rules for cybersecurity and artificial intelligence. Basis: Congressional Research Service summary, version updated 2026-06-29, read at the bill page.
records.sourceOrg: Congressional Research Service

records.text: Main Street Capital Access Act (H R 6955): Loosens rules on banks. New banks get three years to build up their required financial cushion, some rural banks can hold a smaller cushion, regulators must weigh how much their rules burden banks, and several size limits move up so more banks are exempt from fees, reports, and merger approvals — including letting some bank mergers go ahead without checking whether they reduce competition. Basis: Congressional Research Service summary, version updated 2026-07-20, read at the bill page.
records.sourceOrg: Congressional Research Service

records.text: Continuing Appropriations Act, 2027 (H R 9770): A stop-gap spending bill. It keeps the federal government funded — mostly at last year's levels — until December 4, 2026, or until the regular spending bills pass, whichever comes first. Without it the government would shut down when the budget year starts October 1. It makes exceptions for a few programs (like WIC food aid, disaster relief, the Indian Health Service, and wildfire fighting) and extends several expiring programs, including flood insurance. Basis: Congressional Research Service summary, version updated 2026-07-29, read at the bill page.
records.sourceOrg: Congressional Research Service

records.text: Stop Insider Trading Act (H R 7008): Bars members of Congress — and their spouses and dependent children — from buying stock in individual companies, and requires public notice 7 to 14 days before they sell stock they already own. Broad investments like widely held funds are exempt. Breaking the rules brings a fine of at least $2,000 or 10% of the trade (plus any profit made), which can't be paid with campaign money. Basis: Congressional Research Service summary, version updated 2026-07-17, read at the bill page.
records.sourceOrg: Congressional Research Service

records.text: Congressional budget for fiscal year 2027 (H CON RES 113): Congress's budget blueprint for 2027 (with targets through 2036). It doesn't spend money itself — it sets the overall numbers for spending, taxes, and debt, and tells four House committees to write follow-up legislation allowed to increase the deficit by set amounts. That follow-up uses a fast-track process the Senate can't filibuster. Basis: Congressional Research Service summary, version updated 2026-07-30, read at the bill page.
records.sourceOrg: Congressional Research Service

records.text: War Powers resolution on hostilities against Iran (H CON RES 89): Orders the President to pull U.S. armed forces out of hostilities against Iran unless Congress declares war or votes to authorize the use of military force. It says this doesn't stop the U.S. from defending itself, its forces, its diplomatic buildings, or allies from imminent attack. Basis: Congressional Research Service summary, version updated 2026-04-27, read at the bill page.
records.sourceOrg: Congressional Research Service

records.text: Removing Barriers to Work for Disabled Americans Act (H R 8884): Lets the Social Security Administration restart pilot programs — paused since 2022 — that test changes to disability benefits meant to help people on disability work more without losing income. Joining a pilot is voluntary, a participant's total income can't go down because of it, and the agency must tell Congress about each pilot 120 days before starting it. Basis: Congressional Research Service summary, version updated 2026-06-26, read at the bill page.
records.sourceOrg: Congressional Research Service

The CARES Act (March 2020): The first pandemic relief law: $1,200 payments to most adults, expanded unemployment benefits, and forgivable loans to keep small businesses paying staff. records.text: The American Rescue Plan (March 2021): The second big pandemic package: $1,400 payments, an expanded child tax credit that paid parents monthly for a year, and money for vaccines, schools and state governments. Selection criteria: Major legislation that became law (plus one pending measure, marked), and consequential Senate confirmations, since 2020 — chosen before looking at how anyone voted.

records.text: The Infrastructure Investment and Jobs Act (2021): About $550 billion in new money for roads, bridges, water pipes, rural broadband and the electric grid, spread over five years. records.text: The Bipartisan Safer Communities Act (2022): The first major federal gun law in about 30 years — tougher checks for buyers under 21, money for state red-flag programs and school mental health. Still in effect; the under-21 provisions expire in 2032 by the law's own terms. Selection criteria: Major legislation that became law (plus one pending measure, marked), and consequential Senate confirmations, since 2020 — chosen before looking at how anyone voted.

records.text: National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2027 (H R 8800): The yearly military policy bill. It says what the Department of Defense (and the Energy Department's nuclear-weapons programs) may spend money on for the 2027 budget year — which aircraft and ships to buy, how many people serve in the military, pay and health care rules for troops, how the Pentagon buys things, how it works with other countries, and rules for cybersecurity and artificial intelligence. Basis: Congressional Research Service summary, version updated 2026-06-29, read at the bill page.
records.sourceOrg: Congressional Research Service

records.text: Main Street Capital Access Act (H R 6955): Loosens rules on banks. New banks get three years to build up their required financial cushion, some rural banks can hold a smaller cushion, regulators must weigh how much their rules burden banks, and several size limits move up so more banks are exempt from fees, reports, and merger approvals — including letting some bank mergers go ahead without checking whether they reduce competition. Basis: Congressional Research Service summary, version updated 2026-07-20, read at the bill page.
records.sourceOrg: Congressional Research Service

records.text: Continuing Appropriations Act, 2027 (H R 9770): A stop-gap spending bill. It keeps the federal government funded — mostly at last year's levels — until December 4, 2026, or until the regular spending bills pass, whichever comes first. Without it the government would shut down when the budget year starts October 1. It makes exceptions for a few programs (like WIC food aid, disaster relief, the Indian Health Service, and wildfire fighting) and extends several expiring programs, including flood insurance. Basis: Congressional Research Service summary, version updated 2026-07-29, read at the bill page.
records.sourceOrg: Congressional Research Service

records.text: Stop Insider Trading Act (H R 7008): Bars members of Congress — and their spouses and dependent children — from buying stock in individual companies, and requires public notice 7 to 14 days before they sell stock they already own. Broad investments like widely held funds are exempt. Breaking the rules brings a fine of at least $2,000 or 10% of the trade (plus any profit made), which can't be paid with campaign money. Basis: Congressional Research Service summary, version updated 2026-07-17, read at the bill page.
records.sourceOrg: Congressional Research Service

records.text: Congressional budget for fiscal year 2027 (H CON RES 113): Congress's budget blueprint for 2027 (with targets through 2036). It doesn't spend money itself — it sets the overall numbers for spending, taxes, and debt, and tells four House committees to write follow-up legislation allowed to increase the deficit by set amounts. That follow-up uses a fast-track process the Senate can't filibuster. Basis: Congressional Research Service summary, version updated 2026-07-30, read at the bill page.
records.sourceOrg: Congressional Research Service

records.text: War Powers resolution on hostilities against Iran (H CON RES 89): Orders the President to pull U.S. armed forces out of hostilities against Iran unless Congress declares war or votes to authorize the use of military force. It says this doesn't stop the U.S. from defending itself, its forces, its diplomatic buildings, or allies from imminent attack. Basis: Congressional Research Service summary, version updated 2026-04-27, read at the bill page.
records.sourceOrg: Congressional Research Service

records.text: Removing Barriers to Work for Disabled Americans Act (H R 8884): Lets the Social Security Administration restart pilot programs — paused since 2022 — that test changes to disability benefits meant to help people on disability work more without losing income. Joining a pilot is voluntary, a participant's total income can't go down because of it, and the agency must tell Congress about each pilot 120 days before starting it. Basis: Congressional Research Service summary, version updated 2026-06-26, read at the bill page.
records.sourceOrg: Congressional Research Service

The CARES Act (March 2020): The first pandemic relief law: $1,200 payments to most adults, expanded unemployment benefits, and forgivable loans to keep small businesses paying staff. Selection criteria: Major legislation that became law (plus one pending measure, marked), and consequential Senate confirmations, since 2020 — chosen before looking at how anyone voted.
records.sourceOrg: congress.gov bill text and official summary

records.text: The American Rescue Plan (March 2021): The second big pandemic package: $1,400 payments, an expanded child tax credit that paid parents monthly for a year, and money for vaccines, schools and state governments. Selection criteria: Major legislation that became law (plus one pending measure, marked), and consequential Senate confirmations, since 2020 — chosen before looking at how anyone voted.
records.sourceOrg: congress.gov bill text and official summary

records.text: The Infrastructure Investment and Jobs Act (2021): About $550 billion in new money for roads, bridges, water pipes, rural broadband and the electric grid, spread over five years. Selection criteria: Major legislation that became law (plus one pending measure, marked), and consequential Senate confirmations, since 2020 — chosen before looking at how anyone voted.
records.sourceOrg: congress.gov bill text and official summary

records.text: The Bipartisan Safer Communities Act (2022): The first major federal gun law in about 30 years — tougher checks for buyers under 21, money for state red-flag programs and school mental health. Still in effect; the under-21 provisions expire in 2032 by the law's own terms. Selection criteria: Major legislation that became law (plus one pending measure, marked), and consequential Senate confirmations, since 2020 — chosen before looking at how anyone voted.
records.sourceOrg: congress.gov bill text and official summary

records.text: The CHIPS and Science Act (2022): About $52 billion to pay companies to build computer-chip factories in the United States, after the pandemic showed how much depends on chips made elsewhere. Selection criteria: Major legislation that became law (plus one pending measure, marked), and consequential Senate confirmations, since 2020 — chosen before looking at how anyone voted.
records.sourceOrg: congress.gov bill text and official summary

records.text: The Honoring our PACT Act (2022): Extended VA health care and disability benefits to veterans exposed to burn pits and other toxic hazards, and made the government presume certain illnesses were service-related instead of making each veteran prove it. Selection criteria: Major legislation that became law (plus one pending measure, marked), and consequential Senate confirmations, since 2020 — chosen before looking at how anyone voted.
records.sourceOrg: congress.gov bill text and official summary

records.text: The Inflation Reduction Act (2022): Let Medicare negotiate the price of some prescription drugs and capped insulin at $35 a month for people on Medicare, alongside tax credits for clean energy, paid for partly by a minimum tax on large corporations. Selection criteria: Major legislation that became law (plus one pending measure, marked), and consequential Senate confirmations, since 2020 — chosen before looking at how anyone voted.
records.sourceOrg: congress.gov bill text and official summary

records.text: The Respect for Marriage Act (2022): Requires every state to recognize same-sex and interracial marriages performed in other states, so those marriages stay valid even if the Supreme Court changes course. Selection criteria: Major legislation that became law (plus one pending measure, marked), and consequential Senate confirmations, since 2020 — chosen before looking at how anyone voted.
records.sourceOrg: congress.gov bill text and official summary

records.text: The Fiscal Responsibility Act (2023): Ended the debt-ceiling standoff by suspending the borrowing limit into 2025, in exchange for caps on federal spending and new work requirements for some food-stamp recipients. Selection criteria: Major legislation that became law (plus one pending measure, marked), and consequential Senate confirmations, since 2020 — chosen before looking at how anyone voted.
records.sourceOrg: congress.gov bill text and official summary

records.text: April 2024: aid to Ukraine: About $61 billion for Ukraine's defense against Russia's invasion — weapons, ammunition, and economic support. Selection criteria: Major legislation that became law (plus one pending measure, marked), and consequential Senate confirmations, since 2020 — chosen before looking at how anyone voted.
records.sourceOrg: congress.gov bill text and official summary

records.text: April 2024: aid to Israel and humanitarian aid for Gaza: About $26 billion for Israel's military and air defenses, including roughly $9 billion for humanitarian relief in Gaza and other conflict zones. Selection criteria: Major legislation that became law (plus one pending measure, marked), and consequential Senate confirmations, since 2020 — chosen before looking at how anyone voted.
records.sourceOrg: congress.gov bill text and official summary

records.text: April 2024: Indo-Pacific and Taiwan: About $8 billion for military support to Taiwan and other allies in the Indo-Pacific, and for U.S. submarine production. Selection criteria: Major legislation that became law (plus one pending measure, marked), and consequential Senate confirmations, since 2020 — chosen before looking at how anyone voted.
records.sourceOrg: congress.gov bill text and official summary

records.text: April 2024: TikTok divest-or-ban, and sanctions: Required TikTok's Chinese owner to sell the app or have it blocked in U.S. app stores, and added sanctions on Russia, Iran and their weapons suppliers. Selection criteria: Major legislation that became law (plus one pending measure, marked), and consequential Senate confirmations, since 2020 — chosen before looking at how anyone voted.
records.sourceOrg: congress.gov bill text and official summary

records.text: The Social Security Fairness Act (2025): Repealed two rules that reduced Social Security for millions of retired teachers, police, and other public workers, raising their monthly benefits. Selection criteria: Major legislation that became law (plus one pending measure, marked), and consequential Senate confirmations, since 2020 — chosen before looking at how anyone voted.
records.sourceOrg: congress.gov bill text and official summary

records.text: The Laken Riley Act (2025): Requires federal immigration authorities to detain people in the country illegally who are arrested for theft or certain violent crimes, and lets states sue the federal government over immigration enforcement decisions. Selection criteria: Major legislation that became law (plus one pending measure, marked), and consequential Senate confirmations, since 2020 — chosen before looking at how anyone voted.
records.sourceOrg: congress.gov bill text and official summary

records.text: The One Big Beautiful Bill Act (2025): Made the 2017 income-tax rates permanent and added new deductions, while cutting Medicaid and food-stamp spending through tighter eligibility and work rules, and increasing immigration-enforcement funding. Selection criteria: Major legislation that became law (plus one pending measure, marked), and consequential Senate confirmations, since 2020 — chosen before looking at how anyone voted.
records.sourceOrg: congress.gov bill text and official summary

records.text: The GENIUS Act (2025): The first federal rulebook for stablecoins — digital tokens meant to hold a fixed dollar value — requiring issuers to hold real dollar reserves and submit to federal or state supervision. Selection criteria: Major legislation that became law (plus one pending measure, marked), and consequential Senate confirmations, since 2020 — chosen before looking at how anyone voted.
records.sourceOrg: congress.gov bill text and official summary

records.text: The shutdown and the 2026 appropriations that ended it: Reopened the federal government after the longest shutdown on record and funded it for the rest of the year, restoring back pay to federal workers and resuming paused federal payments. Selection criteria: Major legislation that became law (plus one pending measure, marked), and consequential Senate confirmations, since 2020 — chosen before looking at how anyone voted.
records.sourceOrg: congress.gov bill text and official summary

records.text: The 21st Century ROAD to Housing Act (2025): The first broad federal housing law in years: money and rule changes aimed at getting more homes built, plus changes to rental assistance and homelessness programs. Selection criteria: Major legislation that became law (plus one pending measure, marked), and consequential Senate confirmations, since 2020 — chosen before looking at how anyone voted.
records.sourceOrg: congress.gov bill text and official summary

records.text: National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2027 (H R 8800): The yearly military policy bill. It says what the Department of Defense (and the Energy Department's nuclear-weapons programs) may spend money on for the 2027 budget year — which aircraft and ships to buy, how many people serve in the military, pay and health care rules for troops, how the Pentagon buys things, how it works with other countries, and rules for cybersecurity and artificial intelligence. Basis: Congressional Research Service summary, version updated 2026-06-29, read at the bill page.
records.sourceOrg: Congressional Research Service

records.text: Main Street Capital Access Act (H R 6955): Loosens rules on banks. New banks get three years to build up their required financial cushion, some rural banks can hold a smaller cushion, regulators must weigh how much their rules burden banks, and several size limits move up so more banks are exempt from fees, reports, and merger approvals — including letting some bank mergers go ahead without checking whether they reduce competition. Basis: Congressional Research Service summary, version updated 2026-07-20, read at the bill page.
records.sourceOrg: Congressional Research Service

records.text: Continuing Appropriations Act, 2027 (H R 9770): A stop-gap spending bill. It keeps the federal government funded — mostly at last year's levels — until December 4, 2026, or until the regular spending bills pass, whichever comes first. Without it the government would shut down when the budget year starts October 1. It makes exceptions for a few programs (like WIC food aid, disaster relief, the Indian Health Service, and wildfire fighting) and extends several expiring programs, including flood insurance. Basis: Congressional Research Service summary, version updated 2026-07-29, read at the bill page.
records.sourceOrg: Congressional Research Service

records.text: Stop Insider Trading Act (H R 7008): Bars members of Congress — and their spouses and dependent children — from buying stock in individual companies, and requires public notice 7 to 14 days before they sell stock they already own. Broad investments like widely held funds are exempt. Breaking the rules brings a fine of at least $2,000 or 10% of the trade (plus any profit made), which can't be paid with campaign money. Basis: Congressional Research Service summary, version updated 2026-07-17, read at the bill page.
records.sourceOrg: Congressional Research Service

records.text: Congressional budget for fiscal year 2027 (H CON RES 113): Congress's budget blueprint for 2027 (with targets through 2036). It doesn't spend money itself — it sets the overall numbers for spending, taxes, and debt, and tells four House committees to write follow-up legislation allowed to increase the deficit by set amounts. That follow-up uses a fast-track process the Senate can't filibuster. Basis: Congressional Research Service summary, version updated 2026-07-30, read at the bill page.
records.sourceOrg: Congressional Research Service

records.text: War Powers resolution on hostilities against Iran (H CON RES 89): Orders the President to pull U.S. armed forces out of hostilities against Iran unless Congress declares war or votes to authorize the use of military force. It says this doesn't stop the U.S. from defending itself, its forces, its diplomatic buildings, or allies from imminent attack. Basis: Congressional Research Service summary, version updated 2026-04-27, read at the bill page.
records.sourceOrg: Congressional Research Service

records.text: Removing Barriers to Work for Disabled Americans Act (H R 8884): Lets the Social Security Administration restart pilot programs — paused since 2022 — that test changes to disability benefits meant to help people on disability work more without losing income. Joining a pilot is voluntary, a participant's total income can't go down because of it, and the agency must tell Congress about each pilot 120 days before starting it. Basis: Congressional Research Service summary, version updated 2026-06-26, read at the bill page.
records.sourceOrg: Congressional Research Service

records.text: Standing public-comment rules: These standing rules provide a public-comment period. These are the body's published standing rules, not a verified change for a particular meeting.

There is a Public Input section on the agenda, and the Selectboard may keep comment to it. On an agenda item, you may speak when the Chair invites comment on it. On anything else, speak during public comment time — give your name and your topic first; the Chair may put the issue on a future agenda or send it to the Town Administrator rather than take it up on the spot. Newbury is direct about the limit: the public does not have a right to speak at Selectboard meetings unless the Selectboard opens Public Input.
